things.label: Earth
things.description: Loose ground: mineral grit, clay and the material in which roots grow.

things.label: Water
things.description: Flowing, soaking and carrying; a liquid that takes the shape of its container.

things.label: Air
things.description: The invisible moving world around us. It carries moisture and feeds a flame.

things.label: Fire

things.label: Stone

things.label: Sand

things.label: Rain

things.label: Plant
things.description: A living stem with roots and leaves; a source of several different natural materials.

things.label: Fruit
things.description: Ripe, juicy produce with flesh around its seeds.

things.label: Wood

things.label: Flowers

things.label: Plant fiber

things.label: Grain

things.label: Flour

args: Stopped voluntarily after completing stage 5, The mill bend, with advance available. Not stuck and not at campaign ending. Opening clay and brick, the flour-dough-flatbread sequence, bridge building and the portable crossing map were coherent discoveries. Brook was strongest: mostly self-directed construction and a meaningful record of a bridge that stays behind. Plant-to-grain required sampling hinted partners; fruit plus stone failing while fruit plus water made juice was less intuitive. Cottage requested giving a house a window, but window onto house was rejected even though both goals were complete. Mill machinery connected sensibly after making a gear, but water plus wheel failed while water plus planks made a waterwheel. By the end I felt the repeated chain-checklist-advance rhythm more than a changed inhabited place; flour was supplied before the mill existed and I never used the finished mill. I did not feel a reason to revisit earlier areas; automatic travel inventory removed the new crossing map. Five completed scenes felt like enough for this sitting; no universal human-fun claim. Logical-interface only, source blind by protocol, no graphics or touch evaluation.
